source.citation: Moss Engraving Co., New York, 'St. Mary's Church', wood engraving in A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, vol. 1 (Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1884), printed p. 291. The held reproduction is the same engraving, republished by Chicagology.
what_it_does_not_supply: No depicted year, relocation site, scale, measured dimensions or surveyed coordinate.
No evidence that the 1835 church lacked a tower or had this precise belfry. Andreas's text dates the initial no-tower state to construction in 1833 and the addition only to some time afterwards.
No secure proof that the picture shows the post-removal enlargement; assigning it to the 1844 textual state is a declared reconstruction, not a captioned date.
what_it_supplies: Visible form: one long low clapboard range, blank near gable, five tall sash and a door at the far end of the visible long wall; open belfry with curved braces, crossed lower railing, curved pointed cap and cross; one chimney toward the far roof end; boarded sidewalk.
A specific 1884 printed-publication provenance and caption for the held picture.
